item.title: Aday Mara could see NBA debut delayed as old Spanish club threaten Thunder
item.description: As excited as the Oklahoma City Thunder have been about Aday Mara, they're experiencing their first bump on the road. His former Spanish club — Basket Zaragoza — is threatening to take legal action if he suits up for Opening Night and beyond. The team claims he remains under contract with them through the 2026-27 season. Oh wow. That's significant. At least, on paper, it is. Basket Zaragoza has been in contact with the Thunder, NBA and FIBA over the contract dispute. The Spanish club also stated it's prepared to take any necessary legal actions required to ensure he doesn't suit up for OKC. Meanwhile, the Thunder released an official statement in response. Per NBA insider Marc Stein : "Aday last played three years of NCAA college basketball and therefore, as advised by the NBA, no clearance from the Spanish team is required for him to play in the NBA." Mara played with Basket Zaragoza from 2021-23. He then enrolled at UCLA and played two collegiate seasons there from 2023-25. Afterward, he transferred to Michigan for the past collegiate season. That's where he broke out as the eventual No. 12 pick of the 2026 NBA draft. I guess we'll see if anything materializes over this dispute. If I had to guess, I think the Thunder find a way to settle this with Mara's old team. Whether that's ignoring their threats or reaching out for a conclusion. The 21-year-old had a stellar preseason. He's too important to sit out over a small legal dispute like this. This article originally appeared on OKC Thunder Wire: Aday Mara could see NBA debut delayed as old Spanish club threaten Thunder

Adam Davy - PA Images via Getty Images Daniel Dubois vs. Fabio Wardley: WBO heavyweight title Wardley's toughness cannot be questioned after his fight with Dubois. The Ipswich fighter sustained plenty of punishment late in that bout but refused to give up, adamant that he could still turn things around — as he’d done previously in his two prior fights against Joseph Parker and Justis Huni. But how many times can you go back to the well before there's nothing left? For a man with just 22 fights, Wardley has already had a physically demanding career. The wear and tear will be visible on Saturday when Dubois gets his jab going on Wardley's nose, and it busts open again. With just 160 days to heal from such a brutal affair, it’s difficult to imagine Wardley has fully recovered going into the second meeting, nor will he be able to sustain the same amount of punishment. The rematch has likely come too soon for him to be at his best. Wardley is his most dangerous early — and that surely has to be the game plan. Wardley had Dubois down just seconds into their first fight and then put him on the floor again in Round 3. The former champion must believe that if he can jump on Dubois in the opening few rounds and make it a shootout, with his speed advantage and raw power, he has the chance to end things quickly. Dubois was floored both times by overhand rights near the side of his head, which crumbled his balance and saw his legs betray him momentarily. The overhand right is very much Wardley's money punch, and with so much of Dubois' game dictated by his jab, Wardley surely will have plenty of opportunities to land that shot over Dubois' left. That strategy may also put him in harm's way, though. Dubois has ended 22 of his 23 wins inside the distance. He’s a monstrous puncher as well, and if Wardley commits to power shots early, it could leave him open to ferocious counters. In their first fight, Dubois was able to hurt Wardley, but Wardley stood up to the power better. When Dubois was caught by a big shot, he found himself on the canvas; Wardley, however, did not. But will it be the same in the rematch? Has the cumulative punishment had a lasting impact on Wardley's chin, which has been so reliable in the past? There are some comparisons between this rematch and Joe Joyce vs. Zhilei Zhang 2 in 2023. Joyce was the most durable fighter in the division. He had a granite chin and was marketed as an immovable object. Zhang was a devastating puncher, and in their first fight, Joyce stood up to his power until eye damage forced the fight to end prematurely. When they fought the second time, though, Joyce's chin wasn't the same. Zhang forced an early finish with a mammoth right hook. Another similarity to Dubois vs. Wardley 2 was the short turnaround — just five months on both occasions. Joyce was never the same fighter after the first Zhang fight, and I fear that may be the case for Wardley too. As for Dubois, the key for him in this fight will be to stay alert early and settle into a rhythm. Once Dubois can establish himself in the fight and have success with his jab, it will pave the way for him to land his heavier punches on Wardley. The champion needs to weather what will likely be a heavy storm in the opening rounds and try to take over as the fight plays out. Another key advantage in the rematch — just as it was in the first fight — is Dubois' fundamentals, which are much better than those of Wardley. Dubois was a top amateur with numerous youth and junior bouts, while Wardley came up through the white-collar route. Dubois' schooling has led him to be better prepared for the world level of the heavyweight division. It's likely Wardley is not as durable as he was in the first fight, and therefore I see Dubois breaking him down and getting him out earlier this time. item.title: Three In-House Options That Could Save the Bills’ Defense
item.description: If not for Greg Rousseau ’s blocked field goal , the conversation about the Bills’ Week 5 win looks very different. Buffalo rolls out an offense that’s tied for the league lead with 32.8 points per game. On the other hand, the defense has been terrible, allowing 28.2 points per game, which ranks fifth-worst in the NFL. Besides the defensive line holding their own, there aren’t many positives to take away so far. While things have been tough for Buffalo on defense, there is good news. They have a few options in-house that could make big differences the rest of the season. With a mix of both veterans and rookies, it leaves an interesting discussion to be had. Jalon Kilgore Has the Size and Versatility the Secondary Needs Jalon Kilgore, a fifth-round pick this past draft, was immediately met with a lot of intrigue from Bills fans. He was drafted to fill a position where Buffalo lacked depth. Outside of Cole Bishop and C.J. Gardner-Johnson , the options at safety still don’t look great. The Bills’ secondary as a whole has struggled so far this season, which is where Kilgore can help. The South Carolina product brings versatility the defense is missing after Taron Johnson was traded to the Raiders. While Kilgore’s main position is safety, he excels at playing all over the field. Whether he’s at safety or filling in at nickel corner for an injured Dee Alford , he should play. What capacity he plays in isn’t the issue; it’s the fact that he needs to be on the field. With injuries piling up in the secondary, now is the best time for the Bills to see what they have with Kilgore. If they can find a way to have him play a “big nickel” role (or a third safety in a 4-2-5 scheme), there’s no doubt that he can make a difference. At 6-foot-1 and 210 pounds, he has the size to play anywhere effectively. Coverage skills will come with time, but in the big nickel role, he can use his size in the box. He’s not afraid to step up in run support and make a play, something he showed regularly at South Carolina . item.title: Match Preview: Dortmund Back in League Play as They Travel to Union Berlin
item.description: Borussia Dortmund are back in Bundesliga action as they travel to Berlin on Saturday. It’s been a rough week-long stretch for Die Schwarzgelben. First, squandering a two goal lead to Werder Bremen in the Bundesliga last week, followed by a grueling mid-week Champions League defeat in Norway at the hands of Bodø/Glimt. Needless to say, BVB will look to get back on track, sitting in second place in the league due to goal differential with Freiburg. Union Berlin on the other hand have had a torrid start to the season, sitting at 16th in the league. They’ve allowed the second most goals (17) in the league so far this campaign. They did however pick up three points last week after their first win in this year’s Bundesliga campaign, with a 1-0 victory over Elversberg. Momentum for Union Berlin, perhaps? Borussia Dortmund will look to put an end to any glimmer of that. And in the process potentially match a club record 16 points out of a possible 18 after six games (most recently during the 2017/2018 season). Player to Watch: Julian Ryerson The Norwegian missed last week’s clash against Werder Bremen due to a rib injury sustained over international break. He came on in the 60th minute for BVB’s champion’s league clash – in Ryerson’s home country. Now he’ll be closer to full strength, with something to prove against his former side, where he played for over four years. He provides that much needed box-to-box edge from the wing that could impact the game on multiple levels. Plus Nico Schlotterbeck was rested for the midweek European fixture. With him returning, that should solidify the backline more given Ryerson license to make his marauding runs. Niko Kovač’s side can’t afford another slow start. Ryerson provides that burst of energy from the get-go to feed Serhou Guirassy, early and often. Predicted Lineup Score Prediction Union Berlin will be the scrappy homeside and keep this tight for a majority of the match. But I expect Dortmund’s attacking quality to shine through, especially Guirassy. The striker has has an impressive track record against the capital club, with eight goals in eight appearances . Dortmund 3-1 Union Berlin. Your Thoughts? What are your predictions for Saturday’s Bundesliga clash? Will Dortmund right the ship and get back to their winning ways? Let us know in the comments below!

item.description: Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens are “likely” to be without star quarterback Lamar Jackson for the second consecutive week. Jackson, who sprained his left ankle in Baltimore’s win over the Tennessee Titans back on October 4, was not available for the media portion of practice on Friday ahead of the Ravens’ game against the Cleveland Browns this weekend. Jackson has not practiced yet this week, which is a sign that Tyler Huntley is in line to start his second game in a row: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson is not present during media viewing portion of Friday’s practice, which indicates Tyler Huntley will likely start for the second straight week. Jackson missed every practice this week and hasn’t suited up since spraining his left ankle in a win over the… — Jamison Hensley (@jamisonhensley) October 16, 2026 Huntley completed 8-of-9 passes for 63 yards in relief of Jackson in the early October game against the Titans, helping Baltimore salt away a 24-18 victory. As noted by Ravens beat reporter Jamison Hensley above, in his last three starts for the Ravens — all wins — Huntley and the offense have averaged over 33 points. item.title: Tommy Tant Memorial Surf Classic returns to Flagler Beach Oct. 23-25
item.description: The Tommy Tant Memorial Surf Classic returns to Flagler Beach Oct. 23–25, bringing three days of competition, a memorial paddle-out and fundraising for local students and surfers. The 24th annual event will take place just south of the Flagler Beach Pier, with 19 divisions for surfers of all ages and skill levels, according to organizers. The Tommy Tant Memorial Surf Classic returns to Flagler Beach Oct. 23–25, bringing three days of competition, a memorial paddle-out and fundraising for local students and surfers. The 24th annual event will take place just south of the Flagler Beach Pier, with 19 divisions for surfers of all ages and skill levels, according to organizers. The contest began in 1999 in memory of local surfer Tommy Tant, who died unexpectedly the previous year at age 24. Surfing supports scholarships Organizers said the event has raised more than $200,000 for the community over the years. Its current efforts support student scholarships and a Fellows Program that provides grants to help local professional surfers advance their careers. A new exhibition Saturday afternoon will feature professional surfers using a Jet Ski tow to gain speed and launch aerial maneuvers. “My brother was a big supporter of my career, so it’s exciting to watch our Fellows Program grow into its second year and to celebrate it with two of our Fellows in the Tow-At session,” said event director Will Tant, Tommy’s younger brother. Weekend schedule Competition begins Friday, Oct. 23, and continues through Sunday, Oct. 25. A kickoff party is scheduled for 7 p.m. Friday at Craeft Surf Studio, across from the contest site. It will feature live and silent auctions and an acoustic performance by Timing Belt. Other activities include raffles, live painting and a memorial paddle-out scheduled for midday Sunday. An awards ceremony will follow Sunday evening at Craeft Surf Studio, which organizers describe as the event’s new permanent home. AdventHealth physicians will also be on-site to help athletes stretch and prepare between heats. item.title: ‘That’s Just Motivation’ — Jaguars WR Parker Washington Opens Up on Receiving Compliment From NFL Legend Tom Brady
item.description: ‘That’s Just Motivation’ — Jaguars WR Parker Washington Opens Up on Receiving Compliment From NFL Legend Tom Brady Parker Washington has 352 receiving yards and four touchdowns through five games of the Jacksonville Jaguars’ 4-1 start, and his two-touchdown afternoon against the Philadelphia Eagles in London drew praise this week from Tom Brady, a fellow sixth-round pick who went on to win a record seven Super Bowl titles. What Tom Brady Saw in Parker Washington Brady’s comments came in the latest edition of his NFL power rankings for Fox Sports, where he kept the Jaguars at No. 5. He said Washington is no longer just a fun story but a true competitor, and he pointed to the sixth round as the place teams look when they need talent. That round is what links them: New England took Brady 199th overall in 2000, and Jacksonville picked Washington out of Penn State at No. 185 in 2023. Washington earned the mention in the 19-17 win on Oct. 11 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. He caught six of his nine targets for 124 yards, and both of Trevor Lawrence’s touchdown passes went to him. His 51-yard catch opened the scoring in the first quarter, and his 27-yarder with 3:20 left put Jacksonville ahead 16-14. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Jake Elliott’s field goal gave the Eagles a 17-16 lead with eight seconds remaining, and Cam Little won it with a 57-yard field goal as time expired. Brady also credited the Jacksonville defense, which held the Eagles to 22 rushing yards. Washington didn’t hold back about what the compliment meant to him: “That means everything, you know, get recognition from one of the greats. I mean, it’s true, one of the best, you know, so really great quarterback. You know, that’s just motivation to just keep going.” “Special players in that round, you know, so let’s keep it going,” Washington said about being a sixth-round pick, same as Brady. Washington’s next test comes on Sunday, when the Jaguars, first in the AFC South, face the Houston Texans at Wembley Stadium in London. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator The 24-year-old wideout set career highs in 2025 with 58 catches for 847 yards and five touchdowns, and he returned two punts for scores. Five games into this season, Washington’s receiving yards rank 14th in the NFL, and his touchdown catches are tied for fourth. Washington is currently ranked 12th on PFN’s WR Impact Metric with a grade of 82.7. Last season, he ranked 25th with a grade of 77.3. Jaguars general manager James Gladstone said in early September that the team was open to continuing extension talks with Washington during the season. But with Washington’s value rising, he may have more incentive to wait until the offseason, when his performance could put him in a position to seek a deal closer to the upper tier of the wide receiver market. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Aston Villa’s interim boss Sørensen to remain in role for the season
item.description: Aston Villa’s interim boss Sørensen to remain in role for the season Aston Villa have announced the news that Brian Sørensen will remain in his position of interim head coach for the whole of the 2026/2027 season. The Villans revealed the news in an official club statement earlier today. The 46-year-old stepped up from his usual role of women’s technical advisor into the interim head coach role following former boss Natalia Arroyo’s departure at the end of last month. Aston Villa opted for a managerial change following a difficult start to the season. Since taking up his interim position, Sørensen has guided Aston Villa to a 3-1 victory over Newcastle United in the Subway Players Cup along with a 1-1 home draw with Crystal Palace in the Barclays Women’s Super League. The Dane will now be tasked with helping The Villans climb the Barclays Women’s Super League table. Aston Villa face a gruelling nine-match window before the next international break at the end of November. They will face six opponents in the Barclays Women’s Super League, along with three games in the Subway Players Cup. Two of the nine games are against Second City rivals Birmingham City. Aston Villa resume Barclays Women’s Super League action on Sunday afternoon when they play host to Liverpool at Keys Park in Hednesford.

item.title: Braves add Brett Wisely to 40-man roster and outright DaShawn Keirsey Jr.
item.description: TAMPA, FLORIDA - FEBRUARY 26: Brett Wisely #0 of the Atlanta Braves hits a single in the fifth inning against the New York Yankees during a Grapefruit League spring training game at George M. Steinbrenner Field on February 26, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Braves have been making some small and quiet moves with their roster since their elimination in the NLDS and here’s another one. After they selected Danny Young’s contract last week, the Braves have decided to do the same with Brett Wisely as well. DaShawn Keirsey Jr. ended up getting outrighted to Triple-A Gwinnett as a corresponding move so they made a decision on him at some point without publicizing it. All of this was found on the Braves’ transaction page and was reported initially by Harrison Smajovits of Atlanta Braves on SI. More #Braves activity – Brett Wisely was selected to the MLB roster – DaShawn Keirsey Jr. was outrighted to Triple-A – Luke Williams elected free agency after being outrighted to Triple-A — Harrison Smajovits (@HarrisonSmaj) October 15, 2026 Wisely didn’t make any appearances with the Braves at the big league level in 2026 as he ended up playing 125 games for the Gwinnett Stripers this season. He had himself a pretty solid year at the plate, as he hit .281/.399/.436 with 11 home runs and 127 wRC+ at the Triple-A level last season. That’s to say that I’d imagine that the Braves aren’t bringing him up at this point in the offseason because they figure that he’s part of their big league plans for 2027. Wisely has never really been able to translate his Triple-A success to big league success, so I’m guessing that the Braves figure that this is a good way to make sure that they’ll keep their options open with him being used in another transaction down the road, since putting the veteran on the 40-man roster means that he won’t be able to use his rights as a minor league vet to elect free agency. Wisely’s last stint with the big league Braves lasted all of 4 games and nine plate appearances in 2025, in case you’re wondering whether or not there’s really something here. Either way, it’s a totally procedural move that gives the Braves a chance to do something with Wisely from a transactional standpoint going forward during the offseason without potentially losing him for completely nothing. We’ll see how it goes, though.

item.title: John Lynch says George Kittle asked him if the 49ers were trading for a pass rusher
item.description: Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch was asked if trade talks around the league are increasing and whether there are more calls in a Friday morning interview on KNBR : “Just because the flow of the way the trade deadline is approaching, yes. That’s our job to do that. To talk with our counterparts around the league. We receive calls. We make calls. Just to kind of see where the market is at. I think the answer to that is yes. We’re just doing our jobs.” When asked if Lynch could tell us if he was talking to the Los Angeles Chargers about Khalil Mack, he laughed and said: “No, I can’t tell you that. I had a lot of people ask me that yesterday. We seem to be connected to everyone. I don’t know where that comes from. I had a player ask me that yesterday. It’s usually [George] Kittle. He asks about everything, which I love.” Khalil Mack is an obvious trade candidate for the 49ers. Mack said himself that San Francisco was this close to acquiring him in a trade way back in 2018 before the Chicago Bears swooped in at the last minute. Mack wouldn’t cost two first-round picks this time around. Depending on the salary retention, he could cost as low as a conditional Day 3 pick. The Chargers have little reason to hold on to the 35-year-old pending free agent at 0-5. Mack’s $10 million signing bonus has already been paid, so the 49ers would owe a little more than $6 million in 2026 salary. If you’re the 49ers, why not go younger? Mack’s teammate, Tuli Tuipulotu, is in the final year of his rookie deal. He was a second-rounder from the 2023 NFL Draft. On 10 fewer pass-rush snaps, Tuipulotu has five more pressures and a pass-rush win rate that’s five percentage points higher. He also has seven more run stops and forced two fumbles. Tuipulotu is 266 pounds, so he has no trouble holding up against the run. If the 49ers are looking at one of the Chargers’ pass rushers, the lesser-known name might be the better option.

We’re just doing our jobs.” When asked if Lynch could tell us if he was talking to the Los Angeles Chargers about Khalil Mack, he laughed and said: “No, I can’t tell you that. I had a lot of people ask me that yesterday. We seem to be connected to everyone. I don’t know where that comes from. I had a player ask me that yesterday. It’s usually [George] Kittle. He asks about everything, which I love.” Khalil Mack is an obvious trade candidate for the 49ers. Mack said himself that San Francisco was this close to acquiring him in a trade way back in 2018 before the Chicago Bears swooped in at the last minute. Mack wouldn’t cost two first-round picks this time around. Depending on the salary retention, he could cost as low as a conditional Day 3 pick. The Chargers have little reason to hold on to the 35-year-old pending free agent at 0-5. Mack’s $10 million signing bonus has already been paid, so the 49ers would owe a little more than $6 million in 2026 salary. If you’re the 49ers, why not go younger? Mack’s teammate, Tuli Tuipulotu, is in the final year of his rookie deal. He was a second-rounder from the 2023 NFL Draft. On 10 fewer pass-rush snaps, Tuipulotu has five more pressures and a pass-rush win rate that’s five percentage points higher. He also has seven more run stops and forced two fumbles. Tuipulotu is 266 pounds, so he has no trouble holding up against the run. If the 49ers are looking at one of the Chargers’ pass rushers, the lesser-known name might be the better option.

item.title: Chelsea captain Reece James faces lengthy absence following surgery
item.description: Chelsea captain Reece James has undergone surgery -Credit:Marc Atkins, Getty Images Reece James faces a THREE-MONTH spell on the sidelines after undergoing knee surgery. James, 26, missed Chelsea's last two games either side of the international break with an injury that forced him to withdraw from the England squad last month. The Blues captain now looks unlikely to feature again before the new year. Chelsea confirmed on Friday that James has undergone a minor knee operation after sustaining the injury during a training session. A club statement read, via The Mirror : "Reece has already begun his road to recovery and will be supported by the club's medical department at Cobham during this rehabilitation phase. Everyone at Chelsea wishes Reece a speedy recovery and will support him on his road to return." Wrexham shouldn't push the panic button yet despite challenge facing Phil Parkinson Cristiano Ronaldo delivers brutal Portugal 'ultimatum' after Jorge Jesus 'broke his word' -Credit:Darren Walsh, Chelsea FC via Getty Images James previously suffered a knee injury in 2022, which saw him miss that year's FIFA World Cup. The defender's fitness improved last season, allowing him to play a prominent role for England at the 2026 edition. Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has deployed James in midfield this season and on Friday described his absence as 'disappointing'. "It's not going to be a two or three-week thing, it's going to be longer and after that we will see," Alonso told a pre-match press conference ahead of Saturday's match away to Everton. "Before Christmas, after Christmas, time will tell. Things have to be done properly so that he feels right and is in the best possible condition. "It's a disappointment for everyone, for him, but we need to have a squad to deal with injuries. We support him, he will stay close to the team, he's a great influence even when he's not available, and we wish him the best recovery." To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE James' injury comes at a challenging period in the schedule for the Blues. Following their clash with Everton, Chelsea welcome Tottenham Hotspur before hosting Manchester United, sandwiched around a Carabao Cup trip to Liverpool. Levi Colwill has assumed the captaincy at Chelsea since James was ruled out, and Alonso is confident he has sufficient leaders within his ranks. "We have Moi (Moises Caicedo), we have Levi, we have players who take responsibility and carry that role in a perfect way," the Spaniard stressed. "They have the support from the rest and the players respect them when they wear the armband, so it's no bother. Their own personality. Each one is different. Levi is different from Reece, Moi is different, Cole [Palmer], Hendo (Jordan Henderson). "Each one is different, Dibu (Emiliano Martínez) as well. That's why it's so important for me to have a mix of personalities, qualities and stages of their careers. I think we're in a good place in that way."

item.title: When should fighters stop fighting?
item.description: For some, fighting is a business; make as much money from the sport as possible, and then walk away with your health intact. For others, fighting is a lifestyle; it’s a drug that you can’t just quit. There is a tendency to disregard new-age combat sports as a clown show. He doesn’t seem to have one; fighting is simply his purpose. “I don’t live a motivational life, motivation will leave you tomorrow,” Romero says through an interpreter. “It’s something that’s in my blood, it’s something that we do. I was born with the concept of: if you want to be a great athlete, you’ve got to be disciplined. It is my first battle.” Romero won’t be hanging up the gloves any time soon, it seems. item.title: Why Tigers are clear winners of Tarik Skubal trade with Dodgers
item.description: Why Tigers are clear winners of Tarik Skubal trade with Dodgers originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Tigers had a very disappointing 2026 MLB season. Coming into the year, the Tigers were supposed to be postseason contenders, and there was hope they'd be able to make a run in what could've been Tarik Skubal's last year with the team. However, they struggled once Skubal went down with an elbow injury and fell far enough out of the playoff race that the Tigers decided to sell, shipping Skubal out in a deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers . Trading Skubal was not a very popular decision, but now, following the Dodgers' NLCS elimination and the report from ESPN's Alden Gonzalez , the Tigers appear to be the clear winners of this Skubal trade. Tigers are winners of Tarik Skubal trade with Dodgers Gonzalez shared that, with the looming MLB lockout on December 1, "it would be really difficult for the Dodgers to justify signing Skubal to a massive deal before knowing what MLB's economic model will look like." So, with the Dodgers facing an uncertain future regarding how MLB payrolls work, the Dodgers might have to refrain from signing Skubal to a long-term deal. That means he might be leaving the Dodgers in free agency. Skubal might sign elsewhere, and a return to the Tigers could be in play. They do need starting pitching, and it would be quite the move to sign Skubal to an extension and also get the huge trade package for him at the MLB trade deadline that they got from the Dodgers. Zyhir Hope, Brady Smith, and River Ryan were the three players the Tigers got from the Dodgers in the Skubal trade. If even one of them were to turn into a quality big-leaguer, it wouldn't matter what Skubal does in free agency; it would be a win. MORE : How Mets could have advantage over Dodgers in free-agent pursuit of Tarik Skubal But, adding on the context that the Dodgers might not have the means to sign Skubal to an extension, they would've gotten just two-and-a-half months out of Skubal, failing to make the World Series, let alone winning a game in the NLCS. The Dodgers spent a fortune to acquire Skubal from the Tigers, and now he might leave the team after the Dodgers came up well short on their quest to three-peat as World Series champions. One thing should be clear following the NLCS loss for the Dodgers. Regardless of what happens with Skubal in free agency, the Tigers clearly won this trade. It might not have been a popular one for the fans at the time, but it was clearly the right decision, especially with the Dodgers failing to win the World Series in 2026. item.title: Justin Ishbia addresses Chicago railyards deal backlash, warns of cost of inaction
item.description: Justin Ishbia and Rate Field (Getty) For the first time, Justin Ishbia, the owner-in-waiting of the Chicago White Sox, spoke in a public forum about his controversial plan to place the team in his new megadevelopment at an Amtrak railyard. The White Sox currently play in Bridgeport at the publicly-owned Rate Field. In order to move the team’s home games to his new development , dubbed the Railyards, Amtrak needs a new maintenance facility and has chosen Bridgeport as its site. Needless to say, Bridgeport residents are less than thrilled about potentially losing their baseball team and in return, receiving a potentially noisy train maintenance facility just a few blocks away. While acknowledging the community pushback, Ishbia said that there’s also a cost to inaction at a Crain’s event in Fulton Market. According to the outlet, Ishbia noted that furious responses to big real estate gambles are at least partially to blame for the Bears not getting their downtown stadium in 2024 and now potentially moving across state lines to Indiana. He also encouraged residents to consider the benefits of local rail infrastructure. Ishbia’s plan for the Railyards development is contingent on Amtrak being able to move their maintenance facility to Bridgeport. Amtrak plans to use a federal exemption to be allowed to build the $900 million new facility in Bridgeport, rendering a significant chunk of the backlash a moot point. Ishbia still needs certain approvals from the City Council in order to pursue his full vision for the Railyards. Ishbia declined to fully commit to moving the White Sox, at least until he gains full control of the franchise. “I would say it’s not a foregone conclusion — the White Sox leaving. That’s a Jerry [Reinsdorf] decision. Period. End of conversation. One day I’ll have a turn, but it’s not today,” Ishbia said at the event, according to the outlet. Recently, Ishbia revealed plans for the Railyards that included renderings of a new ballpark for the White Sox. — Hunter Cooke Read more Aldermen are ratcheting up pressure on Amtrak and Ishbia’s development plan. item.title: FSU vs. Miami: Score predictions, analysis from FSU Wire
item.description: The FSU Seminoles (3-3, 1-2 ACC) are back on the road, playing the Miami Hurricanes in their toughest game of the season. The Seminoles have not won a road game since 2023 and are looking to snap a two-game losing streak against the Hurricanes. While anything can happen on the football field, it will be tough for FSU to pull off the upset . Miami (5-0, 3-0), the No. 3 team in the country, is simply better at every position and has solidified itself as the top team in the ACC with a 5-0 start. They have the best offense and defense in the conference, with Heisman candidates Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney leading the offense. The defense might not have as much star power, but their defensive front is once again excellent, and they have the ability to easily pressure the quarterback, thanks to defensive ends Marquise Lightfoot and Damon Wilson II. It will be up to FSU's offensive line to have a good game to try and keep Ashton Daniels upright with room to work in the pocket. The Seminoles trail Miami 33-37 all time, and the two are tied 29-29 since they started playing every year. FSU has a winning record in Miami, going 21-20. Here are our predictions for FSU's game against Miami. Matthew Lenix Prediction: Miami 38, FSU 17 I don't see this game being particularly close. Miami has one of the best run defenses in the nation, which will likely force FSU to be one-dimensional, and their offense leads the country in scoring, which is a bad matchup for an inconsistent Seminoles' defense. Florida State will come out inspired, but Miami is just a better team. Brandon Foster Prediction: Miami 38, FSU 20 I think Florida State hangs around longer than the spread might suggest. Rivalry games tend to get weird, and FSU should come into this one with plenty of emotion after the way last week ended. Still, Miami feels like the safer pick right now. The Hurricanes are at home, they are the best team Norvell has faced this season, and Florida State has not shown enough consistency defensively for me to call the upset. Jacob Smith Prediction: Miami 67, FSU 3 Darian Mensah is playing like a Heisman-level QB, but Miami hasn't played anyone to warrant being considered No. 3. JD McCarthy Prediction: Miami 45, FSU 17 These two historic rivals are not on the same level right now, and Mario Cristobal and the Hurricanes will take the chance to hammer that home on Saturday night. The Seminoles have not won on the road since the 2023 season and are outmatched at every position on the field. Look for Malachi Toney and Darian Mensah to have another big game against a weak FSU secondary. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) Getty Images Last year saw the return of the popular golf event call the Skins Game. What used to be a staple for golf fans during the offseason stopped abruptly in 2008 returned in 2025 for Black Friday viewing. This event brings together four PGA Tour pros to compete in a friendly but high-stakes competition with a total purse of $4 million dollars. The latest iteration of the event saw the following golfers competing for big money: 2025 Skins Game Participants Keegan Bradley Xander Schauffele Shane Lowry Tommy Fleetwood For those who don’t remember how things panned out in 2025, Keegan Bradley took home the biggest chunk of the purse, winning 11 skins for a total prize of $2.1 million, while Tommy Fleetwood earned $1.7 million, and Shane Lowry managed to win one skin for $200,000. If you do your math, you would realize the purse money was exhausted with the above golfers, which meant Xander Schauffele was left with a big fat $0 at the end of the event. The event’s rebirth was deemed a success, and the 2026 field has been finalized with the event just over a month away. 2026 Skins Game Details Date: Nov. 27, 2026 Where: The Atlantic Fields Club Location: Hobe Sound, Florida Participants: Justin Thomas Wyndham Clark Brooks Koepka Jackson Koivun How to watch: Amazon Prime Video Time: 9:00am EST Purse: $4 million dollars As for the format of the event, the Skins Game is going back to its roots. The competition itself will return to the original format, which started back in 1983. Last year they tried the “reverse purse” twist, in which each player started with $1 million and the amount went up or down based on whether a player won or lost a hole. item.title: Real Madrid’s Vinícius Jr. appeal rejected
item.description: Real Madrid’s Vinícius Jr. appeal rejected La Liga giants Real Madrid have on Friday been dealt a blow on the personnel front. This comes amid confirmation that the club’s appeal to have Vinícius Jr’s suspension overturned has been rejected. Wide-man Vinícius was of course hit with a heavy sanction on the part of the Spanish football authorities earlier this week. After being shown a straight red card for pulling the hair of Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba during a La Liga clash last weekend, the 26-year-old was banned for four domestic fixtures. Of the collective opinion that this was too severe, the Real Madrid board, in turn, launched an appeal to have the number of games reduced. As alluded to above, however, on Friday, Los Blancos have officially seen their plea rejected. As per a report from journalist Fabrizio Romano: ‘Real Madrid appeal for Vini Jr’s 4-games ban in La Liga has been rejected.’ The Brazilian is therefore primed to sit out all of his side’s upcoming fixtures against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander and Valencia. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Evanilson, Rayan and Rodríguez goals seal Bournemouth’s historic home win in Europe
item.description: An impossible dream realised: the Vitality Stadium staging European football, where the Europa League is becoming an oasis for Bournemouth. No wins yet in the Premier League, but beating Sturm Graz following up winning away at Real Sociedad should calm the domestic pressures mounting on Marco Rose. A pair of Brazilians secured club history, with Evanilson’s first-half header followed by Rayan’s later drive, a clincher coming just as the Austrian visitors were pushing hard for an equaliser. Álvaro Rodríguez’s stoppage-time penalty extended the celebrations. Flag day at the Vitality. Elvis Presley’s high baritone and Andy Williams’ tenor on the public address system marked a different type of occasion. Bournemouth have come a significant distance. “Minus 17 to European dreams” read a banner in the Steve Fletcher stand, marking the journey from the foot of the Football League to becoming a model, continental club. Milan visit next week, an occasion to further broaden the smile of Bill Foley, Bournemouth’s financier present in the posh seats. “A long time coming,” said Bournemouth’s long-serving captain, Adam Smith. “The fans were up for it, the players were up for it.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.description: Director of football is tarnished by recruitment record and Amorim stint but has received glowing review from above Lisandro Martínez is not naive. At 28, he has experienced plenty in football and knows the causes of success and failure. He has a World Cup winner’s medal , whereas Jason Wilcox has overseen the latest period of mediocrity at Manchester United, during which the focus has fallen more on the team’s performances than the wider reasons behind it. Martínez was not solely speaking for himself when, after United’s defeat at Atlético Madrid, he strongly criticised Wilcox. His views are shared by others at United frustrated by the output from above and who “expect” more from a director of football. Wilcox knows he is under pressure because the inadequate results cannot all be pinned on Michael Carrick, who is working with a squad unable to cope with the rigours of challenging at the top of the Premier League and facing Europe’s elite. item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Winning is not enough for Manchester City to move on from this crisis | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. But consider his assessment of Manchester City’s 3-0 win at Liverpool on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. item.description: What had been billed as a day of reckoning for the Premier League champions turned into a Sunday afternoon stroll Anfield welcomed Manchester City to their new reality, a sullied place where every touch is accompanied by cries of “cheat”, any favourable decision is considered proof of further conspiracy and every victory hollow. The sight of Erling Haaland savouring a statement victory in front of City’s supporters after the final whistle, while chants of “going down” echoed around the rest of the stadium, captured the schism at the heart of this Premier League season. item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘I wanted to depart in the best way possible’: Kieran McKenna on Ipswich exit and future plans
item.description: In an exclusive interview, former Ipswich manager talks of his lasting affection for the club, savouring time out with family and friends and ideas for his next move It was on the Portman Road pitch, bathed in bright early May light while immersed in the relief and joy of a third promotion in five years, that Kieran McKenna realised the moment was right. The thought had flickered earlier in the season that this might be his final campaign at Ipswich, only to be pushed into the subconscious by the Championship’s remorseless grind. “But standing out there, I felt this was probably time,” he says of those moments after QPR had been swept aside and a return to the Premier League assured. “Another big victory, a full stadium, in front of my family and the fans. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
